## Practical systems, built around your business

AI is most useful when it works with the tools, records, and approval process you already have. The
goal is not to add another complicated platform. It is to reduce repetitive work, make information
easier to find, and give the responsible person a clear decision point.

::: {.ai-grid}
::: {.ai-card}
### Operations

Connect calendars, employee hours, payroll preparation, and approved bank-payment workflows.

[Explore operations automation →](/ai/operations/)
:::
::: {.ai-card}
### Customer systems

Improve websites, payment systems, inquiry handling, email drafting, outreach, and historical
contact research.

[Explore customer systems →](/ai/customers/)
:::
::: {.ai-card}
### Bookkeeping support

Categorize transactions, collect receipts, and match financial records with supporting documents for
human review.

[Explore bookkeeping automation →](/ai/bookkeeping/)
:::
::: {.ai-card}
### Research and scientific computing

Apply experience with scientific software, large computing systems, and artificial intelligence
workloads to difficult technical problems.

[Explore research experience →](/ai/research/)

## Experience from research and a real small business

Andrea has worked in scientific computing at the San Diego Supercomputer Center since 2013. His
experience includes high-performance Python, distributed computing, cloud infrastructure,
Kubernetes, and artificial intelligence workflows for research.

He also builds and operates the systems behind the Italian School of San Diego, including
enrollment, calendars, customer communication, payments, employee-hour tracking, and bookkeeping
support.
:::
::: {.ai-policy}
**A clear approval boundary**

Calculations, research, classifications, and drafts may be automatic. Sending, submitting,
scheduling, changing records, and initiating payments require approval from a responsible person.

[Read the responsible AI policy →](/ai/responsible-ai/)
:::
:::
:::

::: {.ai-section}
## Start with one process

A useful first conversation focuses on one recurring task: what comes in, which tools are involved,
where time is lost, and which decisions must remain with a person.
